basis: Parkinsonism and pyramidal degeneration define disease; structural talipes occurs in 10/10. Neurogenic bladder reflects neural dysfunction without established direct urinary damage.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder occurs in 30-79%, but reflects neurologic dysfunction; direct urinary tract damage is not established.

basis: Neurometabolic disease defined by lactic acidosis and developmental impairment; developmental delay in 17/17. Hepatomegaly is occasional (5-29%).

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental impairment and seizures are defining manifestations; developmental delay occurs in 17/17.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency with defining chronic cutaneous disease. Bronchiectasis affects 57/135 (~42%) but is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent respiratory infections.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis (~42%) is separately diagnosed secondary disease; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish intrinsic pulmonary involvement.

basis: Developmental disability, polydactyly and vascular hemangiomas are principal defining features. Structural heart and urogenital defects are only reported, without common frequencies.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hemangiomas are vascular tumors explicitly listed among principal defining features; structural heart defects alone lack frequency evidence.
decisions.dermatologic: none: the record does not establish cutaneous origin or independent skin damage; hemangiomas are assigned to their vascular tissue of origin.

basis: Oral/dental and digital malformations define disease; strabismus occurs in 2/4 (50%). Speech delay in 2/4 may reflect oral structural abnormalities rather than independent neurologic disease.

decisions.neurologic: none: isolated speech/language delay in 2/4 does not establish direct neurologic dysfunction given extensive oral malformations.

basis: Complement-mediated disease defined by renal injury, hemolysis and thrombocytopenia. Direct endothelial injury and microvascular thrombosis are defining, essentially universal vascular involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: direct microvascular endothelial injury and thrombosis define the thrombotic microangiopathy and are essentially universal.

basis: The described syndrome includes a metabolic defect, spastic diplegia, intellectual disability and retinitis pigmentosa; clinical findings affected 3/4 relatives, with biochemical causality uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: primary: spastic diplegia and intellectual disability define the reported syndrome (3/4 relatives); association with the biochemical defect remains uncertain.
decisions.ocular: primary: retinitis pigmentosa defines the reported syndrome (3/4 relatives); association with the biochemical defect remains uncertain.

basis: REN-associated tubulointerstitial kidney disease with defining early hypoproliferative anemia. Hyperuricemia reflects impaired renal urate handling rather than an independent metabolic disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hyperuricemia results from renal urate handling abnormalities; the disease is not defined by a separate systemic metabolic or endocrine defect.

basis: Geotrichum fungal infection has pulmonary, mucosal, cutaneous and disseminated presentations; the supplied evidence does not establish pulmonary damage in at least 30% across the concept.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary disease is a recognized presentation, but a reliable frequency of at least 30% across geotrichosis is not established.

basis: Proteoglycan-linker glycosylation defects underlie defining skeletal, joint and cutaneous connective-tissue abnormalities. Cardiac, ocular and developmental damage varies across subtypes.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic cutaneous connective-tissue abnormalities form part of the group's defining phenotype, although severity varies.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: linkeropathies are inborn defects of proteoglycan glycosylation, establishing a metabolic mechanism beyond the presence of an associated gene.
